click.rationale: Clicks a page element (`Clicks on the provided element`) and can include a page snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`), so it can expose authenticated/intranet page content and attacker-authored page content. The click is delivered to the selected page element (`uid of an element on the page`), which an attacker-controlled page can observe or use to trigger requests.

close_page.rationale: Only closes a browser page (`Closes the page by its index`) and does not advertise returning page content or sending agent-supplied content to a host.

drag.rationale: Drags page elements (`Drag an element onto another element`) and can include a page snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`), exposing private or attacker-authored page content. Drag/drop events are delivered to elements on the current page (`from_uid`, `to_uid`), which an attacker-controlled page can observe.

emulate.rationale: Changes browser/page emulation (`Emulates various features on the target page`) and can set data sent to web pages, especially `extraHttpHeaders` which are `included into every HTTP request originating from the page`, plus observable values such as `geolocation`, `userAgent`, and `viewport`.

evaluate_script.rationale: Runs agent-supplied JavaScript in the target page (`Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the target page`) and returns JSON, so it can read private page data or attacker-authored page data. The advertised example includes network fetch (`async () => await fetch("example.com")`), so it can send agent-supplied data to an agent-chosen host. Execution is in the browser page, not advertised as host code execution.

fill.rationale: Types agent-supplied data into a page control (`Type text into an input`) and can include a snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`), exposing private or attacker-authored page content. The filled `value` is delivered to the selected page element and can be read by an attacker-controlled page.

fill_form.rationale: Fills multiple page controls (`Fill out multiple form elements`) with agent-supplied values and can include a page snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`). This can reveal page content and sends the supplied `elements` values into a page that may be attacker-controlled.

get_console_message.rationale: Gets a console message from the target page (`Gets a console message by its ID`). Console messages may contain private application data and can also be authored by attacker-controlled page JavaScript.

get_network_request.rationale: Inspects network traffic and explicitly includes sensitive headers (`request headers (including 'Cookie')` and `response headers (including 'Set-Cookie')`). Response bodies/headers from attacker-controlled sites are untrusted. Optional file path arguments save bodies locally, making the call state-changing when used.

handle_dialog.rationale: Handles a browser dialog (`use this command to handle it`) and can enter `promptText` into a prompt. A prompt opened by an attacker-controlled page can read that supplied text.

hover.rationale: Sends a hover event to a page element (`Hover over the provided element`) and can include a page snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`), exposing private or attacker-authored page content. Attacker-controlled pages can observe the hover target.

lighthouse_audit.rationale: Audits the target page (`Get Lighthouse score and reports`) and navigation mode `reloads & audits`, so it can request the current page host. Reports about authenticated, localhost, or intranet pages can reveal non-public details, and attacker pages can influence report content. It may write reports to `outputDirPath`.

list_console_messages.rationale: Lists console messages for the page (`List all console messages for the target page`). Those messages can include private application data or attacker-authored text from page scripts.

list_network_requests.rationale: Lists recent page requests (`Lists the most recent requests for the target page`). URLs and request metadata can reveal private account, localhost, or intranet activity; attacker-controlled pages can choose resource/request URLs.

list_pages.rationale: Lists open browser pages (`Get a list of pages open in the browser`), which may include private account, localhost, or intranet URLs/titles. Page titles and URLs can be influenced by attacker-controlled pages.

navigate_page.rationale: Navigates a page to an agent-supplied target (`Go to a URL` and `Target URL`), which makes a request to an agent-chosen URL/host. `initScript` is agent-supplied JavaScript executed on the next navigation.

new_page.rationale: Opens and loads an agent-supplied URL (`Open a new tab and load a URL`, `URL to load in a new page`), making a request to an agent-chosen URL/host.

performance_analyze_insight.rationale: Returns detailed information about a performance insight (`Provides more detailed information`) from a trace of the target page. Such insight data can reveal private page URLs/structure/timing and can be influenced by attacker-controlled pages.

performance_start_trace.rationale: Starts tracing (`Start a performance trace`) and by default reloads the page (`reload` default true), sending a request to the current page host, which may be attacker-chosen through prior navigation. Trace results can contain private page data and be influenced by attacker pages; the exact returned result is not specified, so this is conservative. It can also save raw trace data to `filePath`.

performance_stop_trace.rationale: Stops an active trace (`Stop the active performance trace recording`) and may save raw trace data to `filePath`. Trace results can reveal private page URLs/structure/timing and can be influenced by attacker-controlled pages; exact output fields are not advertised, so this is conservative.

press_key.rationale: Sends key input to the page (`Press a key or key combination`) and can include a snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`). The key input is observable by attacker-controlled pages, and the snapshot can expose private or attacker-authored content.

resize_page.rationale: Changes the page window dimensions (`Resizes the page's window`) to supplied `width` and `height`. Page scripts, including attacker-controlled ones, can observe viewport size changes.

select_page.rationale: Selects/focuses an existing page (`Select a page as a context` and `bringToFront`) but does not advertise returning page content or sending data to a web destination.

take_heapsnapshot.rationale: Captures a heap snapshot to a required local file path (`A path to a .heapsnapshot file to save the heapsnapshot to`). The description does not advertise returning the heap contents into the agent context or sending them to a remote host.

take_screenshot.rationale: Takes a screenshot of the page or element (`Take a screenshot of the page or element`) and, if no `filePath` is supplied, returns it instead of saving it. Screenshots can expose private authenticated/intranet content and attacker-controlled page pixels/text. Optional `filePath` writes locally.

take_snapshot.rationale: Returns a text snapshot of the page (`Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree`) unless saved to `filePath`. It includes page elements and `uid`, so it can expose private page content and attacker-authored page text.

type_text.rationale: Types agent-supplied text into the focused page input (`Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input`). An attacker-controlled page can read the typed `text` and the optional submitted key action.

upload_file.rationale: Uploads local browser-instance files through a page element (`Upload a file through a provided element`, `One or more files paths to upload`), so file contents can be delivered to an attacker-controlled page. It can also include a snapshot (`include a snapshot in the response`), exposing private or attacker-authored page content.

wait_for.rationale: Waits for specified text to appear on the selected page (`Wait for the specified text to appear`), revealing whether text is present on potentially private authenticated, localhost, or intranet pages. It does not advertise returning attacker-authored text beyond the agent-supplied query.

value_conditions.effect: Controls availability of evaluate_script; when disabled, the evaluate_script tool and its SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK effects are removed.
value_conditions.default: enabled unless server configuration says otherwise

notes: All judgements are based only on advertised names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations; no implementation was inspected.

Browser-page reads are treated as capable of reaching the user's authenticated pages, localhost, intranet, and file-like browser-accessible content when the advertised operation returns page, console, network, screenshot, trace, or report data.
Browser interactions and navigations are treated as sinks when they can deliver agent-supplied input or browser requests to attacker-controlled pages/hosts.
